- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., -3%+ over 5 days), reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day for next 7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.6/0.2, 0.8/0.1), model may misalign with sentiment cycles; adjust forecast to match sentiment trend direction.
